column3: Adds repentance joined to repair, so post-act forgiveness is not mere erasure.
Supplies the preceding contrast of failed sacred service, but no reopening route.
Shows mercy alongside enduring limits; it is only a distant boundary parallel.
Repeats the repentance-and-repair pattern, though it largely confirms the earlier card.
Adds the local positive profile of faithful communal service.
Links wrongdoing with a returnable moral failure, indirectly supporting openness after fault.
Directly joins turning and repair after wrong with divine turning and mercy.
Clarifies the local contrast between outward service and committed faith, not 9:27's reopening.
Keeps repentance and seeking forgiveness open after rebuke.
Sets forgiveness and punishment within divine discretion, but without the post-event sequence.
Provides local reward language, secondary to the turn after Hunayn.
Offers only a broad after-displacement pattern, not repentance or mercy.
Adds local acknowledgment of mixed deeds as a live setting for possible divine turning.
Continues the local promise of mercy and approval, but does not explain the turning.

Makes present cessation a threshold for ending conflict and opening forgiveness.

Keeps forgiveness and mercy as distinct but jointly sought responses.
